name: Compound PsyCap Scale
construct: Psychological capital as a higher order construct composed of hope, optimism, resilience and self efficacy, built from open items as a free alternative to the commercial PCQ.
licence: PLOS ONE: "This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License, which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited." The CPC-12R article (Dudasova et al., 2021) and the Japanese validation (Ikeda et al., 2023) from which item wording was taken are also CC BY.
sourceUrl: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9896786/table/tab2 (hope, optimism and self efficacy items) and https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0247114 (original resilience items 7 to 9)

items.text: If I should find myself in a jam, I could think of many ways to get out of it.
Right now, I see myself as being pretty successful.
I can think of many ways to reach my current goals.
I am looking forward to the life ahead of me.
The future holds a lot of good in store for me.
Overall, I expect more good things to happen to me than bad.
Sometimes I make myself do things whether I want to or not.
When I’m in a difficult situation, I can usually find my way out of it.
It’s okay if there are people who don’t like me.
I am confident that I could deal efficiently with unexpected events.
I can solve most problems if I invest the necessary effort.
I can remain calm when facing difficulties because I can rely on my coping abilities.

subscales.name: Hope
subscales.description: Agency and pathways thinking, items drawn from the State Hope Scale.

subscales.name: Optimism
subscales.description: Positive expectations for the future, items drawn from the AFF future orientation questionnaire and the LOT-R.

subscales.name: Resilience
subscales.description: Items drawn from the German Resilience Scale RS-13.

subscales.name: Self-efficacy
subscales.description: Items drawn from the General Self-Efficacy Scale.

scoring: Items rated on a 6 point scale from 1 = strongly disagree to 6 = strongly agree. Subscale and total scores are means of the items (1 to 6); higher scores indicate more psychological capital. No reverse scored items are identified. The authors note that norms have not been established and give no cut offs.
citation: Lorenz, T., Beer, C., Pütz, J., & Heinitz, K. (2016). Measuring psychological capital: Construction and validation of the Compound PsyCap Scale (CPC-12). PLOS ONE, 11(4), e0152892. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0152892
transcriptionNote: The original PLOS ONE article presents the items only as abbreviated labels in Figure 1 (an image) and its S1 Appendix is a different questionnaire, so the full item wording could not be read from the itemsUrl. The hope, optimism and self efficacy items are unchanged in the CPC-12R and were transcribed from Table 2 of the CC BY Japanese validation of the CPC-12R (Ikeda, Hatano, Tanaka and Nakahara, 2023, Frontiers in Psychology, 13:1053601); the 3 original resilience items (replaced in the CPC-12R) were transcribed from the text of Dudasova et al. (2021, PLOS ONE, 10.1371/journal.pone.0247114). Item 12 ends "coping abilities" in Ikeda et al.; the Dudasova quotation was cut at "coping". Item numbering within subscales follows the order in those sources and may not match the original CPC-12 item order. Only the 2 anchor labels are published; intermediate points are unlabelled. No respondent instructions are given in any source.
